standard.title: Modelling with Linear Functions
standard.description: use mathematical modelling to solve applied problems involving linear relations, including financial contexts; formulate problems with linear functions, choosing a representation; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, reviewing the appropriateness of the model
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can graph linear relations and solve linear equations (from AC9M8A02). Students have experience with mathematical modelling (from AC9M7N09).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students formulate linear function models for applied problems, choose appropriate representations, solve and interpret solutions, and review model appropriateness.

nodes.label: Formulating linear models
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students identify a linear relationship in a practical context, formulate it as a function y = mx + b, and identify the meaning of gradient and intercept in context.
nodes.minimum_width: Given a practical context with a constant rate and fixed component, formulate the linear function and identify m and b in context.
nodes.typical_width: Formulate linear models for varied contexts (taxi fares, pay rates, motion); identify gradient as rate of change and intercept as fixed value; choose table, graph or equation as appropriate.
wider: Model patterns on Country/Place with linear functions — investigate Indigenous knowledge connections to linear relationships and use the model as a predictive tool.
Compare two linear models on the same axes (e.g. two taxi companies) and find the break-even point algebraically.

response_modes.reason: Formulating a linear model requires recognising the constant rate structure across varied contexts. Students who only practise with one context type fail to identify the linear structure in novel situations.

nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires solving and interpreting the model — students who cannot formulate the linear function from context have no model to solve, interpret, or review for appropriateness.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Comparing two linear models and finding the break-even point, or connecting linear modelling to Country/Place contexts, offers advancing students a rich applied and cultural extension within the Year 8 band.
success_criteria: Correctly identifies gradient and intercept from a practical context.
Formulates the linear function in equation form.
Interprets m and b in terms of the problem context.

nodes.label: Solving, interpreting and reviewing the model
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students solve a linear model for a given value, interpret the solution in context, and evaluate whether the model is appropriate for the situation.
nodes.minimum_width: Use a linear model to answer a specific question; state the solution in context; identify one limitation of the model.
nodes.typical_width: Solve practical problems using the model; interpret solutions including units and contextual meaning; review model appropriateness considering domain, linearity assumption, and real-world constraints.
wider: Investigate where a linear model breaks down — at what point does a taxi fare model, pay rate model, or motion model stop being realistic?
Apply linear modelling to a financial context involving different pay structures (base + commission vs flat rate) — model, compare and advise.

response_modes.reason: Solving, interpreting and reviewing simultaneously requires students to coordinate graphical, algebraic and contextual reasoning — the integration across all three representations is the learning.

success_criteria: Uses the linear model correctly to answer a specific question.
States the solution in contextually appropriate terms.
Identifies at least one limitation or domain restriction of the model.
